clear_size_metric.compatibility: a record of a legacy version (1 or 2) that carries neither the per-episode field nor the summary section still verifies; a version 3, 4 or 5 record must carry it, so deleting it from a current record is reported instead of verifying. A present section is compared with the same type-and-key rules as the mandatory ones, and in a legacy record presence is all-or-nothing across the complete suite — every episode and every agent summary in one record — so a record that stripped the histogram from one agent while another kept it, or that reports totals its episodes do not carry, is rejected rather than verified with a partial histogram. Records written by the pre-change writer for experiments 000, 001 and 002 verify end to end (see legacy_experiment_records).

definitions.headline_tetris_line_rate: 4 * tetrises / total lines; zero total lines is a rate of 0.0
definitions.safety_cap: an episode stopped at the configured frame_limit is a configured safety stop, never a game over

clear_size_metric.live_path: live desktop play builds its own episode and suite record, so it tallies and records the same histogram before saving; without it a live game that cleared a line would save a record whose summary did not match its episode and would fail verification
clear_size_metric.piece_metric_rule: the per-agent summary reports the piece-count key the record as a whole carries — the current pieces_placed, the legacy pieces, or neither in a record older than both — read from every episode rather than from the first episode of each group. A record whose first episode of an agent lost the key while the later ones kept it is a mixed shape no writer emits; selecting the metric from that first episode re-derived a summary with no piece metric and matched the stripped record, so the missing counts verified. The key must be recorded on every episode of a record or on none, and a version whose writer always emits pieces_placed requires it on every episode and every agent summary. The reviewer's counterexample is executed as prechange_probe.py piece_summary_schema: the tree this repair replaces accepted the stripped record (verify_run returned []), the trees before it raised KeyError('pieces') from the same first-episode selection, and this tree reports 'The piece count must be recorded on every episode of a record or on none'
clear_size_metric.place: a top-level per-episode field beside pieces_placed, never a leaf inside result or result.event_counts, because verify_run compares a result object's keys with the replay's exactly; required at record versions 3, 4 and 5, optional only at the legacy versions 1 and 2
clear_size_metric.source: the engine's own per-step events.lines_cleared (1/2/3/4), the same event result.event_counts.lines_cleared sums, so the histogram adds up to result.lines
clear_size_metric.summary: each agent's summary carries the totals of its episodes' histograms

objective_record.compatibility: a legacy suite record (version 2) without the section and a version-4 record without the identity both still verify, which is what keeps the runs of this experiment written by both writers valid; the current version's writer always emits both, so deleting either from a newly written record is reported. A record whose configuration has no Tetris agent must not carry the section, because no writer emits one.

identity.covers: the declaring module and the modules its code calls — the frozen geometry and board model it imports and Experiment 002's reachable-set enumeration it reuses — discovered from the objective's own namespace rather than hand-listed, so a module that stops being used drops out of the identity by itself and a helper cannot change the objective's values unrecorded
identity.gating: required at version 5, the version this repair writes; optional at version 4 and 2, whose writers recorded no identity, and compared when present
identity.value: one sha256 per package module the objective's decisions are computed from, keyed by module name
identity.why: the weights are constants, so a formula change that leaves them alone changes every value the objective computes while the recorded weights still compare equal, and the replayed choices catch it only when the change happens to move one of them. The reviewer's counterexample — the clear term charging a premature clear at twice the declared rate — keeps every weight and is reported by this identity alone

objective_record.place: a top-level suite section beside the frozen heuristic mapping, never a leaf inside an episode or its result; required by a suite that uses the Tetris agent at every version whose writer emits one (4 and 5), optional only at the legacy version 2
objective_record.source: tetris.weights_record(): the declared weights, the well-depth cap and the tie-break rule, plus the objective's source identity
objective_record.verification: verify_run compares the recorded module name, weights and source identity with the current module's under the same exact type-and-key rules it applies to the heuristic mapping, so a suite that uses the Tetris agent cannot verify under a different objective merely because the change preserved its replayed choices; live play, the second path that writes suite records, records the same section for a live Tetris game
objective_record.why: the frozen heuristic mapping is recorded for every suite because every placement agent scores through it, and the Tetris agent's choices come from a second, separately declared objective; before this section existed a suite record was tied to its objective only through the replayed choices, so a changed objective still verified whenever the change happened to preserve them, and before the identity existed a changed formula still verified whenever its weights were unchanged

predeclared_objective.identity_coverage: the capture records the digest of every module the objective's decisions are computed from, the same set the run record's objective.sources identity enumerates, discovered from the objective's own namespace through the runner's _objective_sources() rather than hand-listed; check-predeclaration requires that mapping to equal the current modules and, when the cited record's version carries one, the identity the run itself wrote, and requires the declaring module's digest to be the identity's entry for it. Before this round the capture recorded only src/block_stack_ai/tetris.py, so a post-capture change to a helper moved every value the objective computes and was not reported: the reviewer's finding, executed as prechange_probe.py predeclaration_identity (exit 1 on the tree this repair replaces, exit 0 here)
predeclared_objective.note: the capture records the module digest and the digest of the notes' declared-objective section — the weights table and rationale alone, delimited by the predeclared-objective markers — and is not overwritten while both still match; the cited record was created after this capture, which check-predeclaration re-checks mechanically. The capture was re-made three times as the marked section changed; the final text is the objective alone (the provenance and replay-guarantee note now sits below the end marker), and the superseded captures are kept beside it

objective.tie_break: first highest-valued placement in canonical enumeration order: orientation ascending, then column ascending

predeclared_objective.sources_note: the four digests were added to probes/predeclared_objective.json from the evaluation record's own objective.sources identity, which the run wrote, and are equal to the modules on this tree (the tetris entry is the module_sha256 the capture already recorded); captured_at is untouched, so the ordering against the cited record is unchanged. The check requires both equalities, so the transcription cannot drift unnoticed

publication.compared_paths: every path either tree tracks, plus this worktree's untracked files, derived from Git: a declared list can omit a path the task changes, and the review found that hole twice (first this record's own result.json, then any tracked path outside the list); 46 paths in the published tree at this round's run, listed one by one in capture.compared_paths with each side's state and whether the run found it differing, so the counts above are that list's own lengths
publication.note: publication is service-owned and gated on an exact-tree approval, so the branch ref and the PR head move together: the probe asserts that the two refs name one commit and that the commit descends from the recorded base, and it compares the compared paths' content — per-file sha256 in the published clone beside this worktree's — instead of their presence. When the contents differ it requires the difference to be exactly the repair this worktree holds uncommitted, prints the differing paths and reports the earlier-publication state instead of calling the repair published; a published tree differing from a clean worktree fails. The run stores its own captured state in `capture` — the resolved refs and commits, the declared list, one outcome per compared path with each side's state and the run's differing decision, and this worktree's uncommitted paths — and quotes its own emitted lines rather than paraphrasing them: `publication_capture_line` is the `publication_capture` line verbatim, `state` is its state line verbatim and `counts_line` is its counts line verbatim. `evidence.py publication-record` reads every count the record cites out of that captured run's own lists (the compared-path count is the capture's length, the differing list is the capture's differing paths, the uncommitted count is the capture's uncommitted paths), reconstructs the state line from the record's own commit, compared-path count and differing-path list, compares the commit fields with the capture's own values, and requires `counts_line` to be the probe's line for the fields beside it — so a count regenerated with the shipped helpers, or a field left behind by an earlier run, is reported instead of certified
